own_solution.law: Newton's second law along the incline with kinetic friction: a = g(sin(theta) - mu_k cos(theta)); kinematics v^2 = 2 a d from rest
assumptions: Coulomb kinetic friction with constant mu_k = 0.1
rigid planar incline, block does not tip

TC3E8.regime: mu_s matters only for whether the block starts to slide, i.e. only if mu_s >= tan(40 deg) = 0.839; 0.35 < 0.839 so the block slides and the kinetic result holds

TE4AF.regime: mu_s matters only for whether the block starts to slide, i.e. only if mu_s >= tan(40 deg) = 0.839; 0.35 < 0.839 so the block slides and the kinetic result holds

notes: a = 9.8*(sin40 - 0.1*cos40) = 9.8*(0.642788 - 0.076604) = 9.8*0.566184 = 5.5486 m/s^2. Base: v = sqrt(2*5.5486*5) = sqrt(55.486) = 7.4489 m/s. T6528/T00F7: the stated 5 m begins after 2 m of sliding from rest on the same incline, so v = sqrt(2*5.5486*7) = sqrt(77.680) = 8.8137 m/s. T1CCB/T6FC4: earlier sliding elsewhere before the block was placed and released from rest has no effect: D. Mass (TFF8B/T3E20) cancels between mg and friction mu_k m g cos(theta) and ma: C. Static friction (TC3E8/TE4AF): K, regime mu_s < tan40 = 0.839. All variants state the same numbers (2 m, 2 kg, 0.35). Reading note: for T6528/T00F7 the base text 'released from rest ... slides 5 m' is reinterpreted by the sentence (the release precedes the 2 m), which the sentences make explicit; not a contradiction. mu_s = 0.35 > mu_k = 0.1 is physically consistent.
